docs.title: vexy-co
docs.text:
vexy-co is the umbrella repository for the Vexy tools that work with large language models. Its GitHub description is "Tools around Large Language Model".

The repository itself holds no code yet. It contains a README, the Apache License 2.0 and a .gitignore, and it is tagged v1.0.0. The working tools live in their own repositories and are documented on their own sites.

docs.title: The tools
docs.text:
Tool What it does Install Documentation vexy-co-model-catalog Downloads the model lists of 40 AI providers and writes them as sorted JSON and plain-text files. Command: vmc. From GitHub; not on PyPI yet vexy.dev/vexy-co-model-catalog vexy-overnight Starts Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI, hands a finished session over to the next assistant, and keeps instruction files such as CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md in sync. Commands: vomgr, vocl, voco, voge, version-bump. pip install vexy-overnight vexy.dev/vexy-overnight

Related projects describes both in more detail and shows how they fit together.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: vexy-co is maintained by Adam Twardoch in the vexyart organisation on GitHub. Changes come in through the usual GitHub flow.

docs.title: Where to send a change
docs.text: You want to… Go to Fix or extend the model catalog tool vexyart/vexy-co-model-catalog Fix or extend the assistant launcher and continuation tool vexyart/vexy-overnight Change this umbrella repository or this site vexyart/vexy-co

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A fork or clone of vexyart/vexy-co.
  • uv installed.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create a branch.

    git switch -c docs-my-change

  2. Edit the page in src_docs/md/. To add a page, create the file and add it to the nav list in src_docs/mkdocs.yml.

  3. Build in strict mode and fix any warning it reports.

    src_docs/build.sh

  4. Look at the result with src_docs/build.sh serve.

  5. Commit the change to src_docs/. Committing the rebuilt docs/ is optional; the Docs workflow rebuilds it after the merge.
  6. Open a pull request against main.

docs.title: Writing conventions for this site
docs.text:
• Each page starts with one # Title line and has no front matter.
  • Headings use sentence case.
  • Commands, file names, flags and identifiers go in code style. Code blocks name their language: bash, toml, json, text.
  • Describe what goes in, what the tool does and what comes out. Follow one concrete example rather than listing every option.
  • State only what the code, the tests or a real run confirm. When a page describes another repository, check the claim against that repository.
  • Link to other pages with relative links (related-projects.md). Links outside src_docs/md/ break the strict build; use the full GitHub URL instead.

docs.title: Documentation build
docs.text: This site is generated from Markdown files in the repository and served by GitHub Pages at https://vexy.dev/vexy-co/.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text: Part Role src_docs/md/*.md The pages you are reading src_docs/mkdocs.yml Site name, URL, theme, Markdown extensions and navigation src_docs/build.sh Runs ProperDocs with the MaterialX theme docs/ The generated HTML site GitHub Pages Serves docs/ from the main branch .github/workflows/docs.yml Rebuilds and commits docs/ after changes

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: • uv on your PATH. The build script uses uvx to fetch the pinned tools; you do not install them yourself.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. From the repository root, run:

    ./build.sh docs

    or, equivalently, src_docs/build.sh.

  2. The script runs properdocs build --strict with these pinned packages:

    Package Version properdocs 1.6.7 mkdocs-materialx 10.1.8 pymdown-extensions 11.0.1

  3. The site is written to docs/, replacing what was there, and an empty docs/.nojekyll is added so GitHub Pages serves the files as they are.

Strict mode turns warnings into errors. A link to a page that does not exist, or a page missing from the nav list in mkdocs.yml, stops the build.

docs.title: Preview while you write
docs.text:
src_docs/build.sh serve

This starts a local server on http://127.0.0.1:8000 and reloads the page when you save a file. Extra arguments are passed to properdocs serve, for example src_docs/build.sh serve -a 127.0.0.1:8001.

docs.title: Automatic rebuilds
docs.text:
The Docs workflow runs on every push to main that changes a file under src_docs/ or the workflow itself, and can also be started by hand from the Actions tab. It:

  1. checks out the repository;
  2. installs uv;
  3. runs bash src_docs/build.sh;
  4. commits docs/ as github-actions[bot] with the message docs: rebuild site [skip ci], if anything changed, and pushes.

So a change to a page goes live after you push the Markdown; you do not need to commit docs/ yourself, though you can.

docs.title: Related projects
docs.text: Two Vexy repositories contain working tools for large language models. Each has its own repository, release cycle and documentation site. This page summarises what each does, so you can pick the one you need.

docs.title: vexy-co-model-catalog
docs.text:
Repository: vexyart/vexy-co-model-catalog · Documentation: vexy.dev/vexy-co-model-catalog

vexy-co-model-catalog answers the question "which models does each provider offer today?". It has a fixed table of 40 providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Mistral, OpenRouter and Together AI. For each provider the table names the API type, the environment variable that holds the API key and the variable that holds the base URL.

What goes in and what comes out:

  1. You export a provider's API key, for example GROQ_API_KEY.
  2. You run vmc fetch groq.
  3. The tool requests <base URL>/models, sorts the response by model ID, and writes two files into the current directory:
    • config/json/models_groq.json, the full response;
    • config/txt/models_groq.txt, one model ID per line.
  4. It records the result in models/extra/failed_providers.json, so later runs can skip providers that keep failing.

Because the output is sorted, two runs against an unchanged catalog produce identical files, and a git diff shows exactly which models appeared or disappeared.

The package also offers a Python API (ModelFetcher, StorageManager, ProviderConfig) and replaces an older single-file script, dump_models.py, keeping its file names.

docs.title: vexy-overnight
docs.text:
Repository: vexyart/vexy-overnight · Documentation: vexy.dev/vexy-overnight · PyPI: vexy-overnight

vexy-overnight drives the coding assistants themselves. It has three jobs.

Starting assistants. vocl, voco and voge start Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI with a fixed set of flags. These flags turn off the assistants' permission and sandbox checks, so read the documentation before you use them.

Handing over between assistants. vomgr install writes hook scripts into ~/.claude/hooks/ and ~/.codex/, and vomgr enable claude registers one as Claude's Stop hook. When Claude stops, the hook:

  1. reads ~/.vexy-overnight/settings.toml, where Claude hands over to Codex by default;
  2. builds a prompt from up to five open - [ ] items in the project's TODO.md;
  3. opens a terminal that starts Codex in the same project with that prompt.

Codex hands back to Claude in the same way.

Keeping instruction files in sync. vomgr rules --sync finds every CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, QWEN.md, LLXPRT.md and .cursorrules below the current directory and links the copies of each name to the most recently changed one.

docs.title: How they fit together
docs.text:
The two tools do not depend on each other. vexy-co-model-catalog tells you which model IDs a provider accepts; vexy-overnight starts the assistants that use those models. Both are written in Python, both are command-line tools built with Python Fire, and both are versioned from git tags.

vexy-co-model-catalog vexy-overnight Main command vmc vomgr Talks to Provider HTTP APIs Locally installed assistant CLIs Writes to The current directory ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.gemini, ~/.vexy-overnight Needs API keys Yes, one per provider (except litellm) No; the assistants handle their own login Python 3.10 or newer 3.10 or newer

docs.text:
The vexy-co repository on the main branch holds the files below. There is no source code, no package metadata (pyproject.toml, package.json) and nothing to install.

docs.title: What the .gitignore tells you
docs.text:
The .gitignore is written for Python work. It ignores, among others:

  • Python byte code and caches: __pycache__/, *.py[codz], .mypy_cache/, .pytest_cache/, .ruff_cache/, .pytype/.
  • Build output: build/, dist/, sdist/, wheels/, *.egg-info/, target/.
  • Virtual environments: .venv, venv/, env/, ENV/.
  • Version files written by build tools: __version__.py, _version.py.
  • Local secrets and settings: .env, .envrc, .pypirc.
  • Any file or directory named external, for material that is kept locally but not published.

So future code in this repository is expected to be Python, packaged with a build backend that writes a version file, as the related tools are.
